newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch- May 14.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch- May 14.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Wednesday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:

** US insurance giant American International Group (AIG) has earmarked about 30 percent of its recently closed $2 billion Asian Infrastrcture Fund-II (AIF-II) for equity investments in India, the Business Standard daily reports.
The paper says the allocation from AIF-II which is the second in a series of Asia specific funds from AIG is expected to around $600-$700 million.

** India's western Maharashtra state said on Tuesday it plans a six-billion-rupee bond issue to finance the purchase of a 30 percent equity stake in a 2,450 MW power plant being built by the U.S.'s Enron Corp.
"We will raise six billion rupees through a private placement of bonds," Chief Minister Manohar Joshi told reporters in Bombay following a weekly cabinet meeting.

** India's scooter giant Bajaj Auto will see sluggish growth in the financial year ended March 31 due to a prolonged industrial slowdown that hit vehicle sales during the period, analysts said on Tuesday.
Results for the 1996/97 financial year are due on Wednesday.

They said the firm -- among the world's largest makers of two-wheel vehicles -- was likely to announce a net profit of 4.5 billion rupees ($125 million), up about eight percent from 4.18 billion in 1995/96.
Bajaj Auto's net profit surged nearly 40 percent in 1995/96 from the previous year. Shares of Bajaj Atuyo ended 3.50 rupees higher at 849.75.
** Thermax Ltd is due to announce results for the year ended March 31, 1997 later on Wednesday.
Thermax shares lost 30.50 rupees to end at 278.0.
MARKETS:
The Indian rupee opened Wednesday at 35.83/84 per dollar, unchanged from Tuesday's close, dealers said.
Quiet trade seen during the day with trading range determined by dollar purchases by Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and State Bank of India they said.
** Shares at Bombay exchanges closed with modest losses on Tuesday, as lack of buying support led to a sell-off in frontline stocks, traders said.
Fund activity was mainly concentrated in select second-tier stocks due to cheaper valuations, they said.
** Bombay's benchmark share index ended 33.29 points, or 0.89 percent down at 3,701.96.
** The National exchange index fell 9.45 points to 1,031.05.
-- Bombay newsroom +91-22 265 9000
